parts:
Hello, Zhian:

When I try to run the code on my computer, R version 3.5.1, poppr 2.8.
```{r}
#library("pegas")
#(nanhwe.full <- hw.test(nancycats, B = 1000)) # performs 1000 permuatations
```
It works fine. 

```{r}
#(nanhwe.pop <- seppop(nancycats) %>% lapply(hw.test, B = 0))
```
it gives an error. "Error in dimnames(ans) <- list(names(y), c("chi^2", "df", "Pr(chi^2 >)")) : length of 'dimnames' [1] not equal to array extent"


How to fix it?

Thanks a lot.

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] (nanhwe.pop <- seppop(nancycats) %>% lapply(hw.test, B = 0))shows error?
parts:
Hello,

I would like to point out one thing: hw.test() is a function from the pegas package, so the question is best directed there.

That being said, I know how to fix this issue. One of the problems is that the warnings don't show up in your output. If they did, they would look like this:

Error in dimnames(ans) <- list(names(y), c("chi^2", "df", "Pr(chi^2 >)")) :
  length of 'dimnames' [1] not equal to array extent

In addition: Warning messages:
1: In hw.test.loci(x = x, B = B, ...) :
  The following loci were dropped (not the same ploidy for all individuals):
fca45
2: In mapply(test.polyploid, y, ploidy = ploidy) :
  longer argument not a multiple of length of shorter

This is due to the fact that population 17 of nancycats was not genotyped for locus fca45. You can circumvent this by adding drop = TRUE to the seppop call:

seppop(nancycats, drop = TRUE) %>% lapply(hw.test, B = 0)

Hope that helps,
Zhian

Hi,

This is failing due to a change in the behavior of pegas (which necessitated the modification already mentioned). I'm afraid I don't have the bandwidth to address this at the moment. I'll submit a bug report to the maintainer of pegas to see if he'll fix it in an upcoming version.

That being said, there are several ways of doing things in R. Try to understand what the R code is doing to the data to get the results you want (in this case, a heatmap) and challenge yourself to come up with an alternative way of creating it. The tutorial is meant only to guide you, not to serve as a surrogate for understanding.

Best,
Zhian
